produces: wireframe/flow diagram, state list, edge-case interaction notes, open design questions

quality_bar.verification_method: schema validation of every wireflow node's type against the spec's declared closed enum (screen/decision/system-action/end)
reference-resolution check (reuses the spec's own reference_resolution rule) asserting every transition edge resolves to a declared node on both ends
graph traversal asserting an error-typed outgoing edge exists per user-input node
graph reachability check asserting every node reaches the terminal node and is reachable from the start node

gates/quality_bar.py:human_comprehensibility_verdict against the role's own docs/issue-<n>/reports/<role>.md record text (gates/human_comprehensibility.py tier-1 structural prose rules: lead paragraph present, citation trailing placement, section size bound, no raw dump, enumeration cap); a record with no human-facing prose section anywhere is exempt (bar-met) -- issue #1623.

recomputation.checked_by: TBD (follow-up — issue-521 out-of-scope note: per-role recomputation enforcement is a follow-up once evidence from real usage shows which roles need it)
recomputation.rule: a flow is not complete until every state's edge_case_variant is populated — error-state-before-happy-path-only (NN/g's must-be), never asserted complete from happy-path states alone.

reference_resolution.rule: every transitions entry must resolve to another state's state_name elsewhere in the same record — graph reference-resolution (issue-515 invariant 2); every flow must contain at least one terminal node_type.

record_spec.source_standard: NN/g wireflows (nngroup.com/articles/wireflows) + UML state-machine notation (uml-diagrams.org) for the closed node-type enum NN/g itself leaves unspecified

use_when.board_condition: a requirements-engineering record landed for a screen/flow-facing requirement AND no interaction-design record exists yet for it
